findings.title: notes:save writes to a path chosen by the renderer
findings.statement: The main-process handler for the `notes:save` IPC channel (main.js:20) passes its `filePath` parameter, the first argument sent by the renderer, as argument 0 of the call at main.js:21. REA resolves that parameter-to-argument flow and links the call target to `writeFile` on the `fs` binding as a candidate; main.js requires `node:fs/promises`, and REA leaves the binding's value unresolved. REA reports zero sender-validation observations. The preload's `notes.save` member forwards its arguments to this channel.
findings.impact: Any script running in the window can create or overwrite any file the application user can write by calling `window.notes.save` with an absolute path.
findings.remediation: Do not accept a path from the renderer. Write to a fixed file under `app.getPath("userData")`, or resolve the requested name against that directory and reject results outside it. Validate `event.senderFrame` in both `notes:*` handlers.

findings.title: BrowserWindow disables webSecurity and the renderer sandbox
findings.statement: The only BrowserWindow (main.js:7) sets the literal webPreferences `webSecurity: false` and `sandbox: false`. Disabling webSecurity removes the same-origin policy for the window. Whether that is exploitable depends on what the window loads, which the static analysis does not establish.
findings.impact: Content loaded from outside the application directory would run without same-origin restrictions in an unsandboxed renderer that can call `window.notes`.
findings.remediation: Remove `webSecurity: false` and set `sandbox: true` unless a documented requirement needs them.

next_probe.rationale: Exercise the window and record every resource it loads; a non-local origin makes this a defect.

findings.title: Which page code calls window.notes.save
findings.statement: REA did not analyze the inline script in index.html, so the Evidence does not show which page code calls `window.notes.save` or where its path argument comes from. This affects how the notes:save defect is reached in normal use, not whether the handler accepts arbitrary paths.

next_probe.rationale: Click #save in a controlled replay and record the notes:save invocation arguments.

findings.title: Preload exposes two named functions, not ipcRenderer
findings.statement: With `contextIsolation: true`, preload.js exposes one contextBridge API, `notes`, as an object literal with exactly the members `load` and `save` and no unknown members. Both members invoke literal channels that pair with main-process handlers; `ipcRenderer` itself is not part of the recovered API.
